canonical_name: pForth -- a portable ANS Forth in C (Phil Burk)
lineage: pForth (1994-, Phil Burk): a portable ANS Forth -- an inner interpreter over a threaded-code dictionary, a data and return stack machine, compiled from C; a concatenative stack-machine runtime
version: github.com/philburk/pforth master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

example.command: echo ': sq dup * ; 7 sq . cr bye' | pforth

human_capability_summary.built_to: run Forth -- a concatenative language where a program is a sequence of words operating on an explicit data stack, executed by a tiny threaded inner interpreter that a compiler can extend at runtime
human_capability_summary.pressure: minimal footprint and self-hosting on bare or tiny machines; the language and its compiler are one small extensible dictionary
human_capability_summary.success_means: Forth definitions compile and execute with correct stack effects; the interpreter is portable across machines

known_human_problem_solved: a small, extensible, self-hosting stack-machine language

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run pforth
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: run Forth -- a concatenative language where a program is a sequence of words operating on an explicit data stack, executed by a tiny threaded inner interpreter that a compiler can extend at runtime
